findings.title: An undiverted course through messenger histories
findings.claim: The repeated sunnah clauses in 17:77 frame prior messenger-sending as an established course whose direction is not changed. Successive missions in 23:44 and repeated divine-sunnah formulas in 35:43, 48:23, and 33:62 place that wording within a wider recurrence of messenger history.
findings.mechanism: The focus's two sunnah occurrences carry the established-way reading around the clause naming messengers sent before the addressee and the final tahwilan negation. The wider formulas repeat sunnat with non-replacement and, in 35:43, tahwilan; 23:44 explicitly links successive dispatches, repeated denial, and aftermath. In 14:13-14, a threat to expel messengers is followed by promised destruction of wrongdoers and settlement after them. Contact between the focus's established course and these wider histories makes the course legible as recurring through varied human episodes without itself being diverted.
findings.reader_payoff: The prior messengers appear within a recurring sequence, and the stated invariance of the course is heard alongside changes in human positions and outcomes.
findings.containment: 17:77 still names the way associated with those sent before the addressee and says no diversion is found for it. The wider links supply repeated wording and selected historical episodes; 14:13-14 is one case, so no identical pressure, expulsion, reversal, or outcome is asserted for every messenger. The connection targets supply exact Arabic without target-side morphology.

epistemic.reason: The focus-to-QAC alignment resolves all 13 analysis words, and the cited wider Arabic directly repeats the sunnah/tahwil formula or describes successive missions. The external connection targets lack target morphology, while two represented reader walks are legacy_unbound, so the cross-surah pattern remains qualified.

findings.title: A shared message carried by earlier messengers
findings.claim: The focus's plural Our messengers can also be heard as a class of message-bearers: 21:25 says each messenger sent before the addressee received the same revealed call to worship, linking the focus's prior-messenger series to a shared proclamation.
findings.mechanism: The carrier rusulina names the human messengers in 17:77. In 21:25, messengers sent before the addressee each receive revelation of a common proclamation; 43:45 also frames those earlier messengers as witnesses. That contact activates the person-as-carrier branch through the focus noun and adds continuity of message to its history of sending.
findings.reader_payoff: The earlier messengers become legible as a relay connected by a shared address across missions.
findings.containment: The focus continues to name people sent before the addressee. The shared proclamation comes from the wider parallel in 21:25; it is not stated as the content of 17:77, and the links do not make every detail of the missions identical.

epistemic.reason: The focus occurrence and branch record directly support the person-carrier reading, and the supplied Arabic in 21:25 and 43:45 grounds the wider contact. Target morphology is not supplied, so this remains a qualified contextual resonance.
